description: Classify a bounded Gaussian integer as prime/irreducible in Z[i] using its axis case or rational norm.

source.title: Gaussian primes
source.algorithm_reference_title: Prime Numbers and Algebraic Number Theory, Lecture 26
source.author: Feras Al Faisal
source.pinned_behavior: For an axis element, require its nonzero absolute coordinate to be a rational prime congruent to 3 modulo 4. For an element with both coordinates nonzero, require the norm a^2+b^2 to be a rational prime. Zero and units are not prime.

contract.definition: Return 1 exactly when a+bi is irreducible (equivalently prime) in Z[i]; return 0 for zero, units, and reducible elements.
contract.overflow_behavior: Reject either coordinate outside the bounded range before absolute value or multiplication. Accepted inputs have norm at most 200000000, so every square, norm sum, divisor product, and loop bound fits signed i64.

input.validation_order: Reject null input, length outside 1..3, any length other than 2, and either coordinate outside -10000..10000 before absolute value, squaring, or classification.

output.meaning: 1 for a Gaussian prime, 0 otherwise, -1 for invalid input

workspace.accounting: Native ports use fixed scalar state for the two coordinates, norm/primality candidate, divisor, and loop bookkeeping; no heap or variable-sized arrays are used. Caller-owned input is excluded.

complexity.primary_time: O(sqrt(a^2+b^2)) worst case, with accepted norm <= 200000000
complexity.independent_time: O(L log log L + pi(L)) sieve setup and O(pi(sqrt(n))) norm checking, with L=14142
complexity.independent_space: O(L) Boolean prime table in the Python reference; not part of native workspace
